statement: The supplied sources define the state feedback gain matrix K through the full state feedback control law u = -K x, which modifies the system dynamics to x_dot = (A - B K) x with closed-loop poles given by det[s I - (A - B K)] = 0. The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive regarding an optimal feedback gain (such as via quadratic form differentiation in a linear-quadratic regulator); they only define the feedback matrix K and compute it via pole placement by equating the closed-loop characteristic polynomial to a desired polynomial, noting that choosing the best K for multi-input systems may use an LQR.

symbols.meaning: complex frequency variable in the s-plane

properties.property: Under full state feedback u = -K x, the closed-loop state dynamics become x_dot = (A - B K) x
properties.why: substituting the linear state feedback law u = -K x directly into the open-loop state equation x_dot = A x + B u

properties.property: Under full state feedback u = -K x, the closed-loop output equation becomes y = (C - D K) x
properties.why: substituting the linear state feedback law u = -K x directly into the open-loop output equation y = C x + D u

properties.property: The closed-loop poles are the roots of the characteristic equation det[s I - (A - B K)] = 0
properties.why: the closed-loop transfer function poles correspond directly to the eigenvalues of the closed-loop state matrix A - B K

properties.property: For single-input systems, equating det[s I - (A - B K)] to a desired characteristic polynomial uniquely determines the elements of K
properties.why: matching corresponding coefficients provides an exact, uniquely solvable system of algebraic equations for the feedback gain elements

properties.property: For multiple-input systems, the feedback gain matrix K that achieves a specified set of closed-loop poles is not unique
properties.why: multiple inputs introduce additional degrees of freedom beyond what is required to satisfy the single characteristic polynomial

assumptions.breaks_when: The plant possesses uncontrollable modes, meaning some eigenvalues cannot be placed arbitrarily by state feedback

assumptions.assumption: The entire state vector x is available and measurable for full state feedback
assumptions.breaks_when: Internal states cannot be measured directly and no state observer or estimator is used

assumptions.assumption: The plant dynamics are linear and time-invariant, represented by constant matrices A, B, C, D
assumptions.breaks_when: The plant exhibits significant nonlinearities or time-varying parameters

failure_modes.mode: Non-unique feedback gain in multiple-input systems
failure_modes.signature: Underdetermined algebraic equations when matching coefficients of the characteristic polynomial to determine K
failure_modes.cause: Multiple inputs provide extra degrees of freedom, rendering pole placement insufficient to uniquely define K without an optimal control criterion such as LQR

failure_modes.mode: Inability to assign desired closed-loop eigenvalues
failure_modes.signature: Equations for the elements of K are inconsistent or leave uncontrollable eigenvalues invariant
failure_modes.cause: The plant fails the controllability condition required for arbitrary pole placement

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so optimal_feedback_gain is recorded as a definition
